verses.text: Awake, awake! Put on your strength, Zion. Put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city: for from now on the uncircumcised and the unclean will no more come into you.
Shake yourself from the dust! Arise, sit up, Jerusalem! Release yourself from the bonds of your neck, captive daughter of Zion!
For Yahweh says, “You were sold for nothing; and you will be redeemed without money.”
For thus says the Lord Yahweh: “My people went down at the first into Egypt to live there: and the Assyrian has oppressed them without cause.
“Now therefore, what do I do here,” says Yahweh, “seeing that my people are taken away for nothing? Those who rule over them mock,” says Yahweh, “and my name is blasphemed continually all day long.
Therefore my people shall know my name. Therefore they shall know in that day that I am he who speaks. Behold, it is I.”
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
Your watchmen lift up their voice, together they sing; for they shall see eye to eye, when Yahweh returns to Zion.
Break out into joy, sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem; for Yahweh has comforted his people. He has redeemed Jerusalem.
Yahweh has made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
Depart, depart, go out from there; touch no unclean thing! Go out from among her! Cleanse yourselves, you who carry Yahweh’s vessels.
For you shall not go out in haste, neither shall you go by flight: for Yahweh will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rear guard.
Behold, my servant will deal wisely. He will be exalted and lifted up, and will be very high.
Just as many were astonished at you (his appearance was marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men),
so he will cleanse  many nations. Kings will shut their mouths at him: for they will see that which had not been told them; and they will understand that which they had not heard.

footnotes.content: Wake up, Zion—put on your strength. This isn't borrowed courage, but the strength that was always yours in the Lord. The promise: holiness is being restored, profaning hands are shut out. When shame weighs on us like dust, He calls us to rise and remember what we truly belong to.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rise from dust—literally and figuratively, this is the summons to shake off captivity's grip. The 'bonds of your neck' name a real thing: slavery that bends you down. Jerusalem hears an invitation not to freedom as chaos, but to the dignity of standing upright again.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sold for nothing, but redeemed without money—this is the mercy of it. No price tag, no debt, no bargaining. The Lord doesn't negotiate with captors; He simply speaks redemption into being. His rescue is a gift, not a transaction.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Egypt and Assyria—the great oppressors of Israel's history, both named here as tyrants without cause. This verse anchors the prophecy in real memory: the captivity isn't random, but woven into the long story of faithlessness and rescue that defines God's people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord grieves not for Himself, but for His people's shame and His own name blasphemed. He asks, 'What do I do here?'—not in helplessness, but as the one who feels the weight of mockery. Love makes us answerable to injustice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My people will know my name—not as distant doctrine, but through experience. This is how we truly know Him: by watching Him act, by seeing His word become real in our own hour. 'Behold, it is I'—the same God who promised, keeping His covenant.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet—a stunning image of a messenger running across high places to bring news of peace and salvation. Every step toward us with good news is beautiful; every herald of God's reign deserves that honor.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The watchmen sing because they see the Lord return to Zion—eye to eye, face to face. Not distant, not hidden. The joy is not just in what they see, but in seeing it *together*, in unity restored. That's what His presence does.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Break into joy—even the waste places are summoned to sing. Comfort has come; redemption is real, not theoretical. The land itself joins the rejoicing because its people are restored. Desolation gives way to the laughter of those who thought they'd lost everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His holy arm is laid bare—no hiding, no shadow. All the ends of the earth see God's salvation at work. This isn't a small, private transaction; it's a display of power and covenant-keeping that reaches everywhere, for all to witness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Depart, depart—leave captivity cleanly, not looking back. Those who carry the Lord's vessels (the holy things, the sacred trust) must be set apart. It's not about snobbery, but holiness: we cannot traffic both in defilement and in what belongs to the Holy One.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Not in haste, not by flight—a different exodus than the frantic one from Egypt. This return is orderly, protected, with the Lord going before and behind. He is our front guard and rear guard; we are held safe on both sides of the journey.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My servant will deal wisely, exalted and lifted up—the turning point where the passage opens toward the Suffering Servant. He acts with wisdom; He is elevated. The servant's path leads not down, but up, though the next verses tell us the cost He pays to get there.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His appearance marred more than any man—a real, historical description anchoring the Suffering Servant's physical torment. The disfigurement is so profound it shocks observers; humanity itself seems altered by what was done to Him. The innocent bears the weight of brokenness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He cleanses many nations; kings see what was never told them—readers today hear an echo in every claim of Christ's redemption, every life transformed not by instruction but by encounter with the One who bore our shame. What they could not hear, they now see in changed hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
